action: Place the probe high in the epigastrium. Angle the probe down. Oblique the transducer slightly counterclockwise.
interpretation: Prepare the probe orientation to align with the pancreatic axis.
Establish a 'sagittal' pancreas image (long-axis view of the organ).

action: Inspect the image for the splenic vein.
interpretation: Use the splenic vein as a primary landmark to confirm proximity to, or direct visualization of, the pancreas.

action: Sweep through the entire organ. Do not capture static images of the splenic vein only.
interpretation: Ensure full coverage to avoid missing pathology that is not visible on a single slice.

action: Scan from the head and uncinate process all the way down to the tail.
interpretation: Visualize the full length of the pancreas anatomy.

action: Attempt to visualize the tail, but acknowledge geometric limitations.
interpretation: Note that the entire tail is often not visible as it dives deep from the epigastric scanning position.

action: Inspect the parenchyma specifically for the pancreatic duct. Trace it through the body.
interpretation: Identify the pancreatic duct running throughout the entire length of the pancreas.
Assess the duct diameter. Apply a 2mm cutoff for normal pancreatic duct measurement.

action: Angle the probe towards the patient's right side.
interpretation: Isolate and visualize the pancreatic head and uncinate process.

action: Inspect the anterior aspect of the pancreatic head.
Inspect the posterior aspect of the pancreatic head.
Upon finding the CBD, rotate the probe to be sagittal relative to the CBD. Elongate the structure.
interpretation: Trace the CBD as it courses into the liver.

action: Rotate the probe 90 degrees so it is in a sagittal plane relative to the patient's body.
interpretation: Obtain transverse (short-axis) images of the pancreas.

action: Sweep through the pancreas while maintaining the sagittal body plane.
interpretation: Use surrounding anatomical structures as landmarks to determine specific location within the pancreas.

action: Identify the aorta posterior to the pancreas.
interpretation: Confirm location in the pancreatic body based on the position of the aorta.

action: Sweep towards the patient's right side until the IVC is visualized.
interpretation: Confirm location in or around the pancreatic head based on the presence of the IVC.
Evaluate the pancreas in the transverse plane.
